intel.t: cost of living, "make stuff cost less," covering rent, utilities, child care and health care.

intel.l: Biggest vulnerability as opponents frame it
intel.t: crime and the 2021 prisoner release settlement, tied by Trump and Whatley to the Zarutska killing, plus a slow Helene response. Fact checkers disproved the early release claim about Decarlos Brown.
the campaign brands Whatley a "Big Oil lobbyist" and ran an ad using Whatley's own dated words that inflation and prices were down; FactCheck.org found the quotes accurate but outdated.
a WRAL and WSOC poll had Cooper 54 and Whatley 40 among likely voters; only 37 percent approved of Trump.
SLF and Old North Action cut North Carolina ad reservations in late September and early October, and Whatley ended TV ads early in October to shift to digital.

bottom: Cooper is running an open seat race for the seat Thom Tillis is leaving, against former RNC chair Michael Whatley. His money is overwhelmingly small dollar and party routed, and he holds a large cash edge. Cooper for North Carolina reported $47.19 million in total receipts through September 30, 2026, including $27.15 million transferred from other authorized committees, and $12.48 million in cash, per NC Political News on October 19, 2026, https://ncpoliticalnews.com/news/fec-cooper-whatley-cash-on-hand-september-2026/. WRAL independently reported $47.2 million raised and $12.5 million in cash, https://www.wral.com/news/nccapitol/roy-cooper-michael-whatley-us-senate-house-congress-fundraising-democrat-republican-october-2026/. Whatley had $916,000.
Three interests combine money with a decision he would vote on:

**Small donors.** The campaign says it raised more than $19.5 million in the third quarter and that more than 95 percent of donations were $100 or less, https://roycooper.com/roy-cooper-raises-more-than-19-5-million-during-third-quarter-of-2026/. This bloc wants cost of living relief, which is his whole message.

**Party and leadership.** The Cooper Victory Fund ties him to the DSCC and the North Carolina Democratic Party, and Senate Majority PAC reserved $31.4 million for him. The lever is Senate control itself.

intel.t: public safety and crime, jobs, take home pay and lower taxes, with Trump's backing.

intel.l: Biggest vulnerability as opponents frame it
intel.t: a D.C. insider and Big Oil lobbyist who left his lobbying career off his bio and still holds utility stock.
Trump's base; Trump and Vance both rallied for him in October, Vance in Hendersonville and Trump in Greenville.
SLF and Old North Action cut North Carolina reservations in late September and early October, and Whatley ended TV ads early to go digital, with $916,000 left at September 30.
WRAL and WSOC had Cooper 54, Whatley 40 among likely voters.

bottom: Whatley is the Trump endorsed nominee for the open Tillis seat. His campaign is small next to Cooper's and leaned on outside money that is now leaving the state. Whatley for Senate reported $13.41 million in receipts including $5.10 million of transfers, $12.50 million spent and $916,101.50 in cash at September 30, 2026, per NC Political News, https://ncpoliticalnews.com/news/fec-cooper-whatley-cash-on-hand-september-2026/. WRAL reported the same $13.4 million and $916,000, https://www.wral.com/news/nccapitol/roy-cooper-michael-whatley-us-senate-house-congress-fundraising-democrat-republican-october-2026/.
The interests with money and a live decision:

**Oil and gas.** He spent more than a decade lobbying for oil and gas interests, helped found HBW Resources in 2009, and was executive vice president of the Consumer Energy Alliance until 2019, per Spectrum News, https://spectrumlocalnews.com/nc/charlotte/news/2026/08/14/michael-whatley-roy-cooper-senate. ConocoPhillips and Marathon CEOs and other energy employees gave at least $150,000 to an affiliated PAC.

**Utilities and data centers.** Voltagrid CEO Nathan Ough gave $250,000 to the Whatley Victory Committee, per WUNC, https://www.wunc.org/elections/2026-02-24/in-north-carolinas-u-s-senate-gop-primary-contenders-try-to-topple-trump-endorsed-candidate. Whatley and his wife hold up to $595,000 of Duke Energy and Dominion Energy stock, per WRAL, https://www.wral.com/news/nccapitol/congress-stock-trading-ban-nc-senate-cooper-whatley-worth-feb-2026/.

D.t: Roy Cooper leads by 13.4 in the forecast and wins 99% of simulations. The cushion is about 593,390 votes; a one point swing is about 22,125 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +7.4 and D +19.3. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.
The polls page average is D +10.8. Your best recent poll is Harper Polling (R) at D +15.0; your worst is Rasmussen Reports at D +6.5. 17 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Wake, a projected net 236,841 votes; Mecklenburg, a projected net 228,320 votes; Durham, a projected net 116,262 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Union, R +10.2, 2.3% of the vote; Johnston, R +8.1, 2.1% of the vote; Cabarrus, D +7.9, 2.0% of the vote; Brunswick, R +11.3, 1.9% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Roy Cooper runs furthest behind in Randolph, Davidson, Rowan. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 75% of voters, 49 to 48, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.73 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 69% of voters, 55 to 42, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.43 points; Voters without a degree, 58% of voters, 52 to 45, where a 5 point gain is worth 2.92 points.

The forecast's worst groups for Roy Cooper: Immigration voters 21 to 76, Small counties 45 to 52, Voters who can afford daily costs 46 to 51. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$12.5M cash against $916K. Spend it early on persuasion television in the battleground counties and keep a reserve for the last week.
